# Independent audit: optimized split weights and their global-cut realization

**PASS.** I read all seven sections of
`candidate d4b2499d695ba5c9`
and its verifier, and reran **13,457 exact checks PASS**. The proof is
analytic; the rational checks supplement rather than replace its scalar
and transport arguments. No repair is needed. Section 4 below records a
distinct additional implementation through the parent's global cuts.

## 1. Optimizer and the continuation-sensitive pointwise inequality

The tangent continuation is positive, decreasing, convex and C1. Its
derivative density `q=max(s,delta)^(-d-1)` is positive continuous, and
the effective denominator `R=f/q` has exactly the stated two branches.
The total endpoint cost is convex and C1, with correct derivative signs
`A'=d integral q_A` and `B'=-d integral q_B`. One endpoint eventually
enters the lower affine branch in each infinite direction, giving actual
coercivity. Thus every minimizing shift has the SAME strictly positive
derivative mass `J` on both endpoints. Equality of the costs themselves
is neither assumed nor needed.

For two upper-branch arguments, the power-mean inequality with exponent
`(d+1)/(d-1)` gives exactly the Jacobian factor in (8). For a mixed pair,
writing `z=(delta+y)/2`, `s=(delta-x)/2` gives `0<=s/z<1` from the
actual midpoint denominator bound. The estimate
`z(1-s/z)^(-d)>=z+ds` is precisely the tangent inequality needed to
recover the LOWER-BRANCH value of `R(x)`. This correctly retains negative
endpoint arguments. Replacing `R` by the original affine denominator
would be wrong on this branch, and the source does not do so.

## 2. Weighted conditional quantiles and domination

The conditional marginal densities of a positive continuous density on
a compact convex face are positive and continuous at interior prefixes.
The lower Hausdorff inclusion used in the proof is valid: first move a
fiber point toward an interior lift of the prefix, then perturb the
prefix inside the resulting interior ball. Compactness gives the upper
inclusion. Boundary-nullness and dominated convergence yield continuity
of the marginal densities and conditional CDFs.

Their triangular inverse maps have positive own-coordinate derivatives,
with telescoping product `J/w`. The arithmetic midpoint map is injective
by its first differing coordinate and is a triangular homeomorphism
onto its recursive open interval domain. Repeated one-dimensional
substitution suffices for its Jacobian identity; no unproved
cross-coordinate differentiability or general area formula is used.

The diagonal determinant inequality has the correct direction. Equal
`q`-masses give the common factor `J` in (12), and the pointwise scalar
inequality then yields the measure domination (13)--(14). Its total
mass is `(A+B)/2` because the endpoint marginals are `q/J` and the
transported weights are `R=f/q`. All normalization factors check.
This is stronger than a total-cost estimate but is not a coupling with
endpoint `f`-weighted probability marginals; the distinction is explicit.

## 3. One coupling, supporting bits and retained defects

The identity (17) is the exact decomposition of
`R_A I_A+R_B I_B` into the average effective denominator, its signed
difference and the source capture bit. The midpoint cap implication
`I_A+I_B>=I_K` holds for the same original ambient halfspace. The simpler
bound (18) follows from `min(R_A,R_B)I_K`, including when the source is
missed. Subtracting the actual uncovered source measure gives (19).
Neither the uncovered measure nor its imbalance defect is dropped.

For inward supporting traces, translating the three abstract faces by
the same positive inward normal displacement preserves the midpoint
identity. The limiting bits are the physical inward bits independent of
the positive speed magnitude. Proper cutting hyperplanes are null in
the face, and pure integer boundary fibers keep their closed capture
bit. The common coupling is not reselected separately for each cap or
signature. Finite normal assignments extend continuously, as required
for the stated actual center-based implementation when `a!=0`.

The `a=0` warning is correct FOR CENTER SHIFTS: changing a center cannot
alter a zero-vector affine denominator. The next implementation has a
different geometric parameter and therefore does not contradict that
warning.

## 4. Additional exact implementation by global supporting cuts

Consider the actual three-fiber midpoint relation at bases `-1,0,1`,
with source `(0,y)`. At a normal with tight support midpoint equality,

    h_K=(h_A+h_B)/2,

any affine support majorant touching the source must have slope
`A_0=(h_B-h_A)/2`, and both endpoint gaps are zero. In
`candidate 6748c967393345b9`, choose
the freely available base-denominator coefficient

    b_0(n)=t_*(n).

Then the global cut evaluates the endpoint denominators as
`1+a.(x-y)-t_*` and `1+a.(x'-y)+t_*`. Its normal speeds at this contact
are exactly `H(n)f(L_A)` and `H(n)f(L_B)`, with source speed `H(n)f(L_K)`.
Thus the ENTIRE optimized split transport and its same-cap defects apply
to this actual global-cut continuation as well.

This construction remains available when `a=0`: `b_0` is an independent
affine base coefficient, not a center displacement divided by `|a|^2`.
For any finite prescribed set of distinct active normals, choose the
optimizing values and extend them continuously, just as in the source.
This proves the finite-contact implementation, not a continuous
optimizer selection over every normal or a global payment inequality.

In arbitrary integer rank, the same argument works for one selected
midpoint pair `z_-=p-v`, `z_+=p+v`: choose a coefficient `b_p(n)` with
`b_p(n).v=t_*`. Additional contact fibers see the same affine coefficient
and contribute their actual costs. One cannot assign unrelated shifts
to several dependent pairs at a single normal without further work.

The source's zero-vector square example has an exact improved cost under
this implementation. With `d=3`, `delta=1`, endpoint face areas `1,9`,
middle area `4`, and `a=0`, set

    t_*=sqrt(3)-1.

The derivative masses agree:

    q(1-t_*)=1=9q(1+t_*).

The endpoint cost is

    f(1-t_*)+9f(1+t_*)
       =(3sqrt(3)-2)+sqrt(3)=4sqrt(3)-2<8.

The unshifted cost was ten, larger than eight. This is an actual
available base-denominator improvement, while the own source field
remains unchanged. For a concrete body realization, take homothetic
axis cubes of side lengths `1,2,3` at the three bases, centered at zero;
their support midpoint relation is tight. A constant `b=t_*` gives the
required global convex cuts and all these facet costs simultaneously.
No claim that this selected source is deepest or that the resulting
path has positive global normalized payment is needed or inferred.

## 5. Independent audit of the quantitative surplus, source Section 8

**PASS.** I separately checked the scalar constants and the measure
transfer, including the tangent branch. The expanded source verifier
was rerun after Sections 8--9 were saved: **19,729 exact checks PASS**.

With `k=d-1`, the even power mean of exponent `(d+1)/(d-1)` has the
quadratic lower bound printed in (21). For `d=2` its normalized even
mean is exactly `1+3r^2/z^2`. For `d>=3`, the exponent lies in `(1,2]`,
so the even mean of the second derivatives is at least its value at
zero. Twice integrating, and then applying Bernoulli to the integer
power `k`, gives the exact coefficient `(d+1)/(d-1)`.

For a mixed tangent/power pair `x=delta-2s`, `y=delta+2r`, the hypothesis
on the midpoint denominator is exactly `r>=s>=0`. Setting `z=delta+r`
gives the actual mean `z-s`, the effective-denominator mean `l=z+ds`,
and half difference `D=ds-r`. The quadratic Bernoulli lower bound in
(22) is valid since `s/z<1`. The weighted Cauchy constant is exactly

    1/C_d + 2d/(d+1) = (3d-1)/(d+1) = 1/c_d.

Thus the remainder in (22) is at least `c_d D^2/z`, and hence at least
`c_d D^2/l`. This proves (20) without excluding the tangent continuation.
The pure power case has the stronger coefficient `C_d>=c_d`.

Under the SAME injective midpoint map, the Jacobian lower bound
therefore yields `mu_K-zeta>=c_d kappa^2 zeta` as a measure inequality,
not just a total-cost comparison. The image is measurable through the
triangular inverse; assigning `kappa=0` off that image is harmless.
Cauchy--Schwarz on an arbitrary Borel captured region gives (24), and
the earlier minimum-denominator cap inequality gives (25). At a whole
supporting coincidence these are the already specified inward-selector
integrals. Their signs and interpretation do not change.

For (26), write the signed imbalance as `e=(R_A-R_B)/(R_A+R_B)`.
Then `int e d zeta=(A-B)/2` and `zeta(F_K)=(A+B)/2`; consequently

    int e^2 d zeta >= (A-B)^2 / [2(A+B)].

This verifies both the coefficient of the squared endpoint difference
and the harmonic-mean rewrite. The source correctly claims no upper
bound on the surplus and no universal positive normalized response.

## 6. Independent audit of the constant-source specialization, Section 9

**PASS.** Suppose `a=0`, `delta=1`, and face areas `alpha>=beta>0`.
For `u=(alpha/beta)^(1/(d+1))`, assign the larger face denominator `u`
and the smaller face denominator `2-u`. Their derivative masses agree
exactly: `alpha q(u)=beta=beta q(2-u)`. The latter denominator is always
on the tangent branch, even when negative; that branch remains positive
and has constant `q=1`. The former is on the power branch. Convexity of
the scalar split cost therefore proves the stated global minimum.

The endpoint costs are `beta u` and `beta(du-d+1)`, so (27) is exact.
The effective denominators are correspondingly `u` and `du-d+1`, and
their difference is `(d-1)(u-1)`. This verifies (28), including `u=1`
and its limiting upper bound. The weighted conditional quantiles here
have uniform endpoint marginals. The cap inequality obtained by using
the smaller effective denominator is exactly (29), with coefficient
`2u/[(d+1)u-d+1]`.

These scalar shifts are physically supplied by the independent affine
base parameter of the global-cut construction. They are not obtained
by changing geometric centers when `a=0`. No comparison with the
one-input continuation or universal payment has been added.
